title: Logging preserves an empty-history seam
statement: Let $B$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with at least one work tape, let $x$ and $s$ be Boolean words, and let $q$ be a state of $B$. Padding the seam configuration that has state $q$ and word $s$ on tape zero, with all other tapes empty, by the logging construction with empty history gives exactly the seam configuration of the logging machine with state $q$ and word $s$ on tape zero.
hypotheses_covered: B has at least one work tape
replaced:
For a machine $B$ with at least one work tape: the logged configuration, with
empty history, of the canonical seam carrying a word $s$ on tape zero equals the
canonical seam of the logging machine's larger tape bank, the added tapes being
blank and stationary.
